Fig. 1 shows a uniform rectangular lamina $ABCD$ of sides $8a$ and $4a$. A square $AGFE$ of side $2a$ and a circle of diameter $2a$ with $BC$ as tangent at its midpoint $H$ are removed from the rectangular lamina.

Find,

figures.legende: Fig. 1 : rectangular lamina ABCD (AB = 8a horizontal, AD = 4a), with the square AGFE of side 2a at corner A and a circle of radius a tangent to BC at its midpoint H.

incertitudes: Question 7 (b) : le résultat imprimé « (124 - 7 pi) a / (52 - 2 pi) » porte un facteur a en trop (une tangente est sans dimension). Le calcul donne tan(angle) = (124 - 7 pi)/(52 - 2 pi) ; le corrigé le démontre et signale que le « a » imprimé est une coquille (le résultat imprimé n'est exact qu'avec a = 1).

Question 7 : sur la figure, AB = 8a est le côté horizontal (étiqueté 8a sur DC, côté opposé) et AD = 4a (2a + 2a) ; H est le milieu de BC, centre du cercle à la distance a de BC. Le filigrane du site est visible sur la figure recadrée, sans gêne pour la lecture.

questions.enonce_markdown: the distance from $AB$ and $AD$ of the centroid of the remainder of the lamina,
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Set-up.** Take axes with origin $A$, the $x$-axis along $AB$ (length $8a$) and the $y$-axis along $AD$ (length $4a$). The lamina is uniform, so mass is proportional to area and the centre of mass coincides with the centroid. Work with areas (the common surface density cancels). The remainder is the rectangle minus the square minus the circle.

| Part | Area | $x$ (from $AD$) | $y$ (from $AB$) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rectangle $ABCD$ | $8a\times 4a = 32a^2$ | $4a$ | $2a$ |
| Square $AGFE$ (removed) | $4a^2$ | $a$ | $a$ |
| Circle (removed) | $\pi a^2$ | $7a$ | $2a$ |
| Remainder | $(28 - \pi)a^2$ | $\bar x$ | $\bar y$ |

For the circle: its radius is $a$ and it touches $BC$ at its midpoint $H = (8a, 2a)$, so its centre is $a$ to the left of $H$, at $(7a, 2a)$.

Area of the remainder: $32a^2 - 4a^2 - \pi a^2 = (28 - \pi)a^2$.

**Moments about $AD$** (sum of area $\times$ $x$): whole $=$ remainder $+$ removed parts, so

$$(28 - \pi)a^2\,\bar x = 32a^2(4a) - 4a^2(a) - \pi a^2(7a) = (128 - 4 - 7\pi)a^3 = (124 - 7\pi)a^3$$

$$\bar x = \frac{(124 - 7\pi)\,a}{28 - \pi}\approx 4.10\,a$$

**Moments about $AB$** (sum of area $\times$ $y$):

$$(28 - \pi)a^2\,\bar y = 32a^2(2a) - 4a^2(a) - \pi a^2(2a) = (64 - 4 - 2\pi)a^3 = (60 - 2\pi)a^3$$

$$\bar y = \frac{(60 - 2\pi)\,a}{28 - \pi}\approx 2.16\,a$$

**The centroid of the remainder is at distance $\dfrac{(124 - 7\pi)a}{28 - \pi}\approx 4.10a$ from $AD$ and $\dfrac{(60 - 2\pi)a}{28 - \pi}\approx 2.16a$ from $AB$.**
themes: centre of mass of composite bodies

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the tangent of the angle of inclination of $AD$ to the vertical when the remainder of the lamina is suspended freely from $D$ in equilibrium is $\dfrac{(124 - 7\pi)a}{52 - 2\pi}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** The lamina hangs freely from $D$ and is in equilibrium: the only forces are the weight (acting at the centre of mass $G$) and the reaction at $D$, so the line $DG$ must be vertical. In the lamina's own axes, $D = (0, 4a)$ and $G = (\bar x, \bar y)$ from part (a).

The line $DA$ points from $D$ straight down the side $AD$. If $\varphi$ is the angle between $DA$ and the vertical line $DG$, consider the right-angled triangle formed by $D$, $G$ and the foot of the perpendicular from $G$ to $AD$:

- horizontal distance of $G$ from $AD$ (opposite side) $= \bar x$,
- distance along $AD$ from $D$ down to the level of $G$ (adjacent side) $= 4a - \bar y$.

$$4a - \bar y = 4a - \frac{(60 - 2\pi)a}{28 - \pi} = \frac{(112 - 4\pi - 60 + 2\pi)a}{28 - \pi} = \frac{(52 - 2\pi)a}{28 - \pi}$$

$$\tan\varphi = \frac{\bar x}{4a - \bar y} = \frac{(124 - 7\pi)a}{28 - \pi}\times\frac{28 - \pi}{(52 - 2\pi)a} = \frac{124 - 7\pi}{52 - 2\pi}$$

Numerically $\tan\varphi = \dfrac{102.01}{45.72}\approx 2.23$, so $\varphi\approx 65.9^\circ$.

**$\tan\varphi = \dfrac{124 - 7\pi}{52 - 2\pi}$.** A tangent is a ratio of lengths and has no dimension: the factor $a$ in the numerator of the printed result is a misprint (the printed expression is correct only in units where $a = 1$).
